procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in for sleep. Lying awake past 2 or 3 am most nights for about two months, even on trazodone; wanted something stronger. Mood lower since winter. Stopped going to therapy around January. Denies SI, intent or plan; no self-harm.

PHQ-9 16, GAD-7 9. Vitals unremarkable. Tired-appearing, linear, no psychomotor change.

A/P:
- Insomnia: not adding a second sedative. Kept trazodone at 50 mg. Went over a fixed wake time, no screens in bed, getting up if awake more than 20 minutes. CBT-I app info given.
- Depression, recurrent, moderate, worse: offered sertraline again or another agent; declines. Encouraged him to call the psychiatry clinic to restart therapy; he has the number. Crisis line reviewed.
- Follow-up in 2 to 3 months.

documents.title: Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. Missed July follow-up.

Says summer was easier. Sleep improved after he started getting up at the same time each day; still uses trazodone, though not every night. No therapy since winter. No SI.

Never smoker, no alcohol. Not working.

Meds: trazodone 50 qhs. NKDA.

Exam: well, mood euthymic-to-low, affect fuller than April. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen benign. No edema. Skin clear.

PHQ-9 10.

Plan: CBC and CMP today since none in two years. Flu and COVID vaccines today. Revisit mood in the spring or as needed.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Asher, your blood count and chemistry panel from the physical are both normal. No follow-up needed for these.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting trazodone 50 mg, 90-day supply. Fill history: last picked up in October. Pt reports he takes it on bad nights only. Pended for PCP.

documents.title: Refill Approved
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent #90, 1 refill. Please get him on the schedule for a mood check, video is fine.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his bedroom, camera on.

Mood 'up and down.' Spends a lot of time at home. Sleep varies; uses trazodone some nights, skips others, refills late. Not in therapy. Denies SI.

PHQ-9 13.

Recurrent depression, moderate, untreated by choice; insomnia on intermittent trazodone. Raised medication and therapy again; he'd rather leave things as they are for now. No change. Reach out any time; check back in the fall.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED
Visit: 09/02/2025, arrived 06:50

CC: erection, painful, about 6 hours

30-year-old man woke with an erection around 1 am that has not gone down. Painful. No injury to the groin or perineum, no illicit drugs, no erectile medications. History of depression; takes trazodone at night. No known sickle cell disease or blood disorder, none in the family.

PMH: depression, insomnia. PSH: none.
Meds: trazodone 50 mg qhs.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, not employed (former maintenance worker).

Vitals: normal throughout.
GU: penile shaft fully rigid and tender to touch. No bruising, laceration or other sign of injury. Glans and corpus spongiosum soft, not engorged. Testes normal.

Labs: CBC and basic chemistries unremarkable. UA normal.
Corporal aspiration: bright red blood. Corporal gas pH 7.40, pO2 96 mmHg, pCO2 39 mmHg, consistent with arterial (non-ischemic) flow.

Course: ice packs and observation, no intracavernosal medication. Gradual detumescence by about 10:45. Pain resolved.

Dx: non-ischemic (arterial) priapism.

Disposition: home. Stop trazodone until reviewed by your primary care physician. Outpatient urology follow-up. Return at once for an erection lasting more than 4 hours.

documents.title: Patient Call After ED Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Was in the ED yesterday morning for a prolonged erection, resolved there with ice and waiting, sent home. Told to stop his trazodone and see urology. Feeling fine now, no recurrence. Instructed: do not take trazodone, return to ED for any erection over 4 hours. Will request the ED record. Visit booked 10/2 with PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-ED follow-up. ED record from 9/2 reviewed: about 6 hours of painful priapism, aspirate bright red with an arterial-pattern gas, settled with ice and observation. CBC, chemistries and UA were normal there.

Since then: no further episodes. Has not taken trazodone since that night. No groin injury he can recall.

Sleep is worse off trazodone, taking an hour or more to fall asleep. Mood low, not hopeless. No SI.

PHQ-9 14. Vitals normal. Comfortable, flat.

A/P:
1. Arterial priapism, one episode, resolved. Trazodone discontinued and should stay off. Urology referral placed as the ED advised.
2. Insomnia: no new sleep medicine today. Gave CBT-I workbook and app info, consistent wake time, limit naps.
3. Depression, recurrent, moderate: offered an antidepressant again; declines. Psychiatry clinic number given again.
4. Flu shot today.
Follow-up in 6 to 8 weeks.

documents.body: Hi Asher, your 11/25 visit is cancelled. Call or message whenever you're ready and we'll find a time. Also, urology hasn't heard from you yet; their scheduling line is on your referral printout.

procedures.procedure: Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, with overnight observation
Visit: 05/12/2026 19:25 to 05/13/2026 10:30

CC: bleeding gums, bruises on arms and legs

31-year-old man brought in by his roommate. Gums bleeding on their own for a couple of days and bruises appearing on his arms and legs. Roommate says he has kept to his room more and more the past few weeks and worries he swallowed something. Patient says he is depressed. On further questions, he had been setting out a store-bought rat poison around the apartment several days ago. Denies prescription medicines or supplements now. Seen here last September for priapism.

PMH: depression, recurrent; insomnia; history of not taking medicines as prescribed; priapism 2025.
Home meds (from prior record): trazodone 50 mg qhs. Patient denies taking any.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: no alcohol. Never smoker.
Family: no bleeding disorders or sickle cell disease.

Vitals within normal limits on arrival and through observation.
Exam: multiple ecchymoses over both upper extremities. Slow oozing at the gum line. No petechiae. Abdomen soft, no liver or spleen enlargement. Neuro intact.

Labs: platelets 180,000/uL. PT 24 s. PTT 61 s. Bleeding time 5 min. Serum tox screen negative for opioids, benzodiazepines and acetaminophen.

Psychiatry consult (evening of 5/12): depressed mood, cooperative. Denies suicidal intent, thoughts of self-harm, or intentional ingestion; describes the exposure as happening while he was putting out the bait. Not felt to need inpatient care. Advised outpatient behavioral health follow-up; resources given.

Course: vitamin K1 10 mg IV. Observed overnight; gum oozing stopped by morning, no new bruising.

Dx: rotenone poisoning, accidental, with coagulopathy.

Disposition: home with roommate. Vitamin K1 5 mg by mouth daily, prescription sent. INR recheck with primary care in a few days. Remove remaining bait from the apartment. Return for any bleeding.

documents.title: Pharmacy Fill Notice
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Fill history update: vitamin K1 (phytonadione) 5 mg tabs filled 5/13/26, prescriber from a regional hospital ED. No ED notification received here. Called pt, no answer, voicemail full. Sent portal message asking him to call. Front desk to request ED records.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to regional hospital HIM for any ED/observation records from May 2026.

documents.title: Patient Returned Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt returned call. Went to the ED earlier this month for bleeding gums and bruises after putting out rat poison at home. Kept overnight, given vitamin K. Says the bleeding has stopped and he's taking the pills. Does not recall being told about a blood test. Advised he needs a visit and an INR check soon. He will call back to schedule once he knows his ride. Asked him to call 911 or go back to the ED for any bleeding.

documents.title: Records Request, Second
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Nothing received from the May request. Re-faxed to the hospital records office and called; they say it is in queue.

documents.title: Need appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: hi can i get an appointment sometime soon. not urgent. still feeling pretty down and not sleeping good

documents.title: RE: Need appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Asher, you're booked Tuesday 9/8 at 10:20 with your doctor. If things feel worse before then, call us, and for a crisis call or text 988.
